messages.content: We’re looking at Naples for six nights late next summer, Saturday through Friday. The two possibilities are August 18–24 or August 25–31, 2029. It would be the two of us from Minneapolis, and I want to see whether a beach hotel is realistic before we get attached to dates.

What is the combined ceiling for flights and hotel, and does ‘beach hotel’ mean directly on the sand or would a short walk work? I’ll also compare Fort Myers with any alternate airport whose airfare savings survive the added drive.
$4,800 total for airfare and hotel. Within a five-minute walk is fine. Nothing is booked, and transfers can sit outside the ceiling for now, but I do want them estimated so we see the real trip cost.

That gives us a clear comparison. I’ll treat both ranges as six nights for two travelers, price economy round trips from MSP, and separate airfare, lodging allowance, and airport transfers. Do you expect to rent a car, or should I model rideshare or a prearranged car to Naples?
No rental car unless it somehow makes financial sense. We expect to stay around the beach and downtown, so start with rideshares. Which airports are actually worth considering?

RSW in Fort Myers is the practical first choice: roughly 35–45 miles from central Naples and commonly about 40–55 minutes without heavy traffic. Miami and Fort Lauderdale can have more flight competition, but each is roughly a two-hour drive, sometimes longer. Tampa is also around 2.5 hours away. For six nights without a car, I would compare RSW seriously and retain FLL only as a price check; MIA and TPA would need unusually large airfare savings.
Okay. Give me high-level numbers for both weeks through RSW and FLL. They can be planning estimates, not pretend live quotes.

For August 18–24, a reasonable planning range for two round trips is $700–$950 via RSW and $520–$760 via FLL. Rideshares round trip are approximately $150–$220 from RSW versus $360–$500 from FLL. That leaves $3,850–$4,100 for six hotel nights through RSW, or about $642–$683 per night including hotel taxes and fees. Through FLL, the airfare-only budget leaves $4,040–$4,280, about $673–$713 nightly, but the higher transfer cost largely consumes that advantage in the real trip total.
And the second week? I’m wondering whether running into Labor Day weekend changes the hotel picture even though we leave Friday.

For August 25–31, I would pencil in $620–$850 for two via RSW and $480–$700 via FLL. The same transfer ranges apply. Your hotel allowance through RSW becomes $3,950–$4,180, or about $658–$697 per night all-in. Through FLL it becomes $4,100–$4,320, or about $683–$720 nightly. Because checkout is Friday before Labor Day, you avoid the peak holiday nights, though Thursday may begin to firm up and inventory could tighten.
So the second week looks a little better. Are those hotel allowances enough for somewhere genuinely close to the beach, or are we still likely to end up inland once taxes and resort fees appear?

They are workable allowances, but they should not be mistaken for room rates. At roughly $660–$700 all-in per night, you can investigate beachfront resorts and strong options within a few blocks of the Gulf. If taxes and resort charges total roughly 20–25%, the corresponding advertised room-rate target is closer to $525–$580. Parking would not matter without a car, but destination fees and mandatory valet policies still need checking.
I’d rather hold some budget back than spend right to $4,800. Can we set a lodging target that gives us room if the flights move?

For the August 25–31 week through RSW, set the hotel target at $3,600 all-in for six nights, averaging $600 per night after all mandatory charges. Using a midpoint airfare estimate of $735, flights plus hotel would be about $4,335, leaving a $465 buffer under the stated ceiling. Estimated RSW rideshares of about $180 would remain separate, putting the preliminary whole-trip figure near $4,515.
That feels more responsible. Compare the same conservative setup through FLL, including the time cost in plain terms.

Using a midpoint FLL airfare estimate of $590 and the same $3,600 hotel target, the capped total would be about $4,190, with roughly $410 in round-trip ground transportation outside it. The whole-trip estimate is therefore about $4,600, around $85 more than the RSW structure despite cheaper flights. It also adds approximately three to four total hours in the car across arrival and departure, with more exposure to traffic delays.
Then FLL isn’t really saving us anything. Is Miami even worth putting on the next search, or can we drop it now?

You can drop MIA for the first detailed search. Its Naples transfer is comparable to or less convenient than FLL, and it would need to beat RSW airfare by roughly $300–$400 for two just to offset added transportation, before assigning any value to the longer drive. If RSW fares later spike, FLL is the better alternate to reopen first.
One correction: I said flight and hotel ceiling, but I don’t want the recommendation to hide the transfers. Keep the $4,800 cap exactly as stated and show the rideshares separately every time.

Understood for this trip: the $4,800 ceiling covers only airfare and lodging. Airport rideshares will be listed separately and included only in a distinct projected trip total. For the stronger structure, that is approximately $735 airfare plus a $3,600 all-in hotel target, or $4,335 against the cap; add about $180 in RSW transfers for a projected $4,515 overall.
Before we settle it, what could make August 18–24 the better week? We have equal flexibility between them.

The earlier week becomes stronger if a specific hotel has a promotion or markedly better room inventory then, or if the later Thursday carries an early holiday-weekend premium. On broad planning numbers, however, August 25–31 has the better airfare outlook and a slightly larger lodging cushion. Weather risk and heat are broadly similar across adjacent weeks, so neither has a meaningful planning advantage there.
Choose the structure for the next round, then. I don’t need hotel names yet, just the dates, airport, budget boundaries, and what we should compare when we start lodging.

Proceed with Saturday, August 25 through Friday, August 31, 2029, flying MSP–RSW round trip for two. Use $735 as the airfare planning midpoint, with $850 as the point at which we should recheck FLL. Target no more than $3,600 all-in for six hotel nights, leaving about $465 within the $4,800 flight-and-hotel ceiling at the midpoint airfare. Keep estimated RSW–Naples rideshares of $150–$220 separate; the midpoint projected trip total is about $4,515. For lodging, compare the true total after taxes and mandatory fees, exact walking time to public beach access, room category, cancellation terms, and whether beach service is included. Nothing is reserved.
